title: HRCT at a glance
intro: Check inspiration and prior studies → identify the dominant pattern → map its distribution → integrate ancillary findings.

branches.title: Reticulation → is there fibrosis?
branches.lead: Look for distortion, traction bronchiectasis and volume loss. Reticulation alone is insufficient.
rows: UIP pattern, if no features suggesting another diagnosis.
Probable UIP, if no alternative features.
Consider NSIP (ground glass, subpleural sparing), HP (air trapping / three-density pattern), or sarcoidosis (upper peribronchovascular fibrosis).
branches.note: UIP describes a pattern. Diagnose IPF only after excluding other causes in clinical / multidisciplinary assessment.

branches.title: Lucencies → true cysts or mimics?
branches.lead: Trace on adjacent slices: airway continuity suggests bronchiectasis; absent walls favour emphysema; subpleural clusters in fibrosis favour honeycombing.
rows: Consider LAM; correlate with clinical context.
Consider pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis, especially in smokers.
Consider Birt–Hogg–Dubé; ask about pneumothorax and renal / family history.
Consider LIP; correlate with autoimmune disease and other causes.
branches.note: Report distribution, wall, shape, size range and associated findings; a few cysts alone do not establish diffuse disease.

branches.title: Other dominant patterns → use distribution
branches.lead: Describe the pattern before naming a disease; mixed patterns are common.
rows: Perilymphatic: sarcoidosis / lymphangitic spread. Centrilobular: small-airway disease / HP. Random: haematogenous spread.
Review onset, distribution and context: infection, oedema, haemorrhage or organising pneumonia are considerations.
Compare vessel size; use expiration to assess air trapping when acquired.
Prone imaging, when acquired, helps distinguish dependent change from persistent disease.
branches.note: Check pleura, nodes, oesophagus and pulmonary vessels for diagnostic clues.

report: Pattern + distribution + extent → fibrosis / cyst features → ancillary findings → interval change → leading diagnosis and alternatives.
